Unitree introduces UniUni for coordinating robot performances

Stage maps, individual timelines and battery monitoring accompany a natural-language choreography demonstration.

Humanoids Daily ↗17 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

One interface for a performance

Unitree presents UniUni as a system for preparing and controlling multi-robot performances. Its video shows natural-language changes to movements, paths and formations alongside a stage map and a separate timeline for each robot.

Choreography and equipment status

Battery levels, temperatures and per-robot emergency stops appear alongside a motion library and LiDAR mapping view. Bringing these together can help operators identify ready performers, while physical-site safety still requires management.

Limits of the demonstration

The promotional video is not a systematic measurement of preparation time or reliability. The announcement cited here does not specify maximum fleet size or the underlying AI model, and it does not establish autonomous cooperation on industrial tasks.
